questions.question: The pectoral region is located on which aspect of the thorax?
questions.explanation: The text defines the pectoral region as the anterior aspect of the thorax.

questions.question: Which of the following structures secretes milk in females?
questions.explanation: The breasts, or mammary glands, are the structures that secrete milk in females.

questions.question: Which landmark is a palpable notch at the upper border of the manubrium sterni?
questions.explanation: The suprasternal notch is located at the upper border of the manubrium sterni between the clavicles.

questions.question: Which landmark marks the junction between the manubrium and the body of the sternum?
questions.explanation: The sternal angle, or angle of Louis, marks the junction of the manubrium and the body of the sternum.

questions.question: The sternal angle serves as a landmark to identify which structure?
questions.explanation: The sternal angle is used to identify the 2nd rib, which helps in counting the other ribs.

questions.question: In males, the nipple usually lies at the level of which intercostal space?
questions.explanation: In males, the nipple usually lies in the 4th intercostal space just medial to the midclavicular line.

questions.question: At what distance below the clavicle can the tip of the coracoid process be felt?
questions.explanation: The tip of the coracoid process is felt in the infraclavicular fossa, 2.5 cm below the clavicle.

questions.question: Which line runs vertically downwards from the midpoint of the clavicle?
questions.explanation: The midclavicular line runs vertically downwards from the midpoint of the clavicle to the midinguinal point.

questions.question: Which line runs vertically downwards from a point midway between the anterior and posterior axillary folds?
questions.explanation: The midaxillary line runs vertically downwards from a point located midway between the anterior and posterior axillary folds.

questions.question: Which nerve supplies the skin above the sternal angle?
questions.explanation: The skin above the horizontal line at the level of the sternal angle is supplied by supraclavicular nerves (C3 and C4).

questions.question: Which intercostal nerves supply the skin below the sternal angle?
questions.explanation: The skin below the horizontal line is supplied by anterior and lateral cutaneous branches of the 2nd-6th intercostal nerves (T2-T6).

questions.question: Which spinal segments form the brachial plexus, leaving a direct meeting point between C4 and T2 dermatomes?
questions.explanation: The nerves derived from C5-T1 spinal segments form the brachial plexus, making the C4 and T2 areas meet.

questions.question: Which muscle is the largest of the pectoral region?
questions.explanation: The pectoralis major is described as the largest muscle of the pectoral region.

questions.question: The clavicular head of the pectoralis major arises from which structure?
questions.explanation: The clavicular head arises from the medial half of the anterior aspect of the clavicle.

questions.question: The sternocostal head of the pectoralis major arises from all of the following except?
options: Medial parts of the 2nd-6th costal cartilages
questions.explanation: The sternocostal head arises from the sternum, costal cartilages, and external oblique aponeurosis, but not the coracoid process.

questions.question: The pectoralis major inserts on which part of the humerus?
options: Medial lip of the bicipital groove
Lateral lip of the bicipital groove
questions.explanation: Pectoralis major inserts by a U-shaped tendon on the lateral lip of the bicipital groove.

questions.question: The twisting of the lower fibres of the pectoralis major forms which structure?
questions.explanation: The twisting of the lowest fibres inserting highest forms the rounded axillary fold.

questions.question: Which nerves supply the pectoralis major?
questions.explanation: The nerve supply is by lateral (C5 to C7) and medial pectoral (C8 and T1) nerves.

questions.question: Which muscles of the upper limb are supplied by all five spinal segments of the brachial plexus?
questions.explanation: Pectoralis major and pectoralis minor are the only muscles of the upper limb supplied by all five spinal segments.

questions.question: The clavicular head of the pectoralis major performs which action on the arm?
questions.explanation: The clavicular head flexes the arm, while the sternocostal head adducts and medially rotates it.

questions.question: The sternocostal head of the pectoralis major performs which action on the arm?
questions.explanation: The sternocostal head adducts and medially rotates the arm.

questions.question: Congenital absence of the sternocostal part of the pectoralis major causes weakness in what movement?
questions.explanation: The congenital anomaly causes weakness in adduction and medial rotation of the arm.

questions.question: The pectoralis minor lies deep to which muscle?
questions.explanation: The pectoralis minor is a small triangular muscle that lies deep to the pectoralis major.

questions.question: From which ribs does the pectoralis minor arise?
questions.explanation: It arises from the 3rd, 4th, and 5th ribs near their costal cartilages.

questions.question: The pectoralis minor inserts into which structure?
questions.explanation: It inserts via a short thick tendon into the medial border and upper surface of the coracoid process.

questions.question: Which action is performed by the pectoralis minor?
questions.explanation: Actions include assisting in protraction, depressing the point of the shoulder, and acting as an accessory muscle of respiration.

questions.question: Why is the pectoralis minor considered the key muscle of the axilla?
options: It is the largest muscle there
It forms the floor of the axilla
questions.explanation: It crosses in front of the axillary artery and is used to divide the artery into three parts.

questions.question: In a prefixed pectoralis minor, the muscle arises from which ribs?
questions.explanation: A prefixed origin means it arises from the 2nd to 5th ribs.

questions.question: A vertical sheet of muscle fibers passing superficial to the medial part of the pectoralis major is called what?
questions.explanation: It is termed the rectus sternalis or sternalis muscle.

questions.question: The anterior lamina of the pectoralis major tendon is formed by which fibers?
questions.explanation: The anterior lamina of the tendon is formed by the clavicular fibres.
